PLUR 101: A Beginner's Guide to Rave Culture

By PLURGASM @plurgasm ⏱ 5 min read

Everyone starts somewhere. Maybe a friend invited you to your first festival and you had no idea what to expect. Maybe you have been curious about rave culture for a while and finally decided to dive in. Either way, welcome. You are in the right place.

This guide covers everything a first-time raver needs to know: what PLUR actually means, how kandi trading works, dancefloor etiquette, and how to have a safe and genuinely amazing time.

What is PLUR?

PLUR stands for Peace, Love, Unity, Respect. It started in the early 90s New York rave scene as both a greeting and a philosophy, and it became the backbone of global rave culture for a reason.

PLUR is not just a slogan. It is how the rave community actually operates at its best:

  • Peace: no judgment, no gatekeeping, no ego. The dancefloor is a judgment-free zone. It doesn't matter what you're wearing, what music you like, or how long you've been going to raves.
  • Love: unconditional love for strangers. The kind that makes someone hand you water when you look overheated, or check on you if you're sitting alone outside a tent.
  • Unity: one crowd, one energy. Every background, every genre preference, every body. The dancefloor erases all of it.
  • Respect: for personal space, for consent, for the music, and for each other. Respect means looking out for people around you.

Kandi: What It Is and How Trading Works

Kandi are the colorful beaded bracelets you will see ravers wearing stacked up their arms. Each one was handmade by someone, worn, and traded. Every piece has a story.

Trading kandi is one of the most beloved rituals in rave culture. It happens through the PLUR handshake, a four-step gesture that physically represents each letter:

  1. Peace: press your flat palms together (like a namaste)
  2. Love: interlock your fingers together
  3. Unity: hook your thumbs together, hands still joined
  4. Respect: slide the kandi bracelet from your wrist to theirs

A few etiquette rules: always ask before initiating. Accept a trade graciously even if the piece isn't your style, because it's about the connection, not the bracelet. Never demand kandi or trade with someone who seems uncomfortable. You can always politely decline.

How to Do the PLUR Handshake

If you've ever watched two ravers press their hands together and swap bracelets, you've seen the PLUR handshake, the little ritual behind trading kandi (the beaded bracelets you'll see all over any show). It spells out the four words the whole scene is built on: Peace, Love, Unity, Respect. Here's how it goes.

  1. Peace: You each make a peace sign and touch your two fingers to theirs.
  2. Love: You each form half a heart with your hand and bring them together into one.
  3. Unity: Press your palms flat together, hands meeting in the middle.
  4. Respect: Interlock your fingers, then slide a kandi bracelet off your wrist and onto theirs.

That's it. The bracelet you pass along is theirs to keep, a small piece of the night that says you're glad they're here. Don't overthink it; everyone's first trade is a little awkward, and that's half the fun.

Dancefloor Etiquette

Rave etiquette is mostly common sense, but here are the things that matter:

  • Watch your space. Festivals are crowded. Be aware of the people around you, especially near the front of stages.
  • Ask before touching. Consent is non-negotiable. Always ask before hugging, dancing with, or touching anyone.
  • Check on people. If someone looks unwell, check on them. If they need help, find a medic. That is what they are there for.
  • Don't push to the front. The people who got there early earned their spot.
  • Leave space for flow artists. If someone is spinning or doing flow arts, give them room. It is genuinely beautiful to watch and dangerous to interrupt.

Safety Basics for Your First Rave

  • Tell someone where you're going and when you expect to be back
  • Go with at least one person you trust
  • Agree on a meeting spot before you go in, because phones die and crowds split groups
  • Drink water. Roughly 500ml per hour if you're dancing
  • Bring earplugs. The music is loud and hearing damage is permanent
  • Know where the medical tent is when you first arrive
  • DanceSafe is at most major festivals. Find them for harm reduction information

What to Wear

Rave fashion is expressive and there are truly no rules, but practically speaking: wear shoes you can stand in for hours, bring a layer if you're at an outdoor event, and if you're in a crowd, wear something you're comfortable moving in.

Kandi, LED accessories, and flow toys are all welcome at most festivals. Check the specific event's rules on what's allowed before you go.

The most important thing: show up with an open mind and genuine respect for the people around you. The rave community is one of the most welcoming on earth when PLUR is actually practiced. We are glad you're here.
